leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eight round-1 configurations are a single-part prize for optical lattice clocks to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. The shared elements are the two names, the argument that independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) compare lattice clocks at about 1e-18, and the view that the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist. Not shared: the weight given to the overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-trap prizes, how far the fundamental-physics reach (redshift over millimetres, constants, dark matter) is demonstrated or still prospective, and whether the citation should be framed around magic-wavelength trapping or around accuracy. Several of these members moved to B052 after reading the openings (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson, Pearce), and Kroll and Lindroth flag that their near-identical openings should not be counted as independent evidence. Support is therefore wide but partly the result of convergence, not of seven independent first choices.

One member prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene to Allan MacDonald, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and Rafi Bistritzer, with B052 listed first among his alternatives and B021 second. His case is a simple, analysable mechanism (the 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction) confirmed by the 2018 experiments, reproduced widely, and opening a tunable field of correlated matter. He concedes the reservations himself (open pairing mechanism, sample variability, omission of Yuan Cao and earlier theory) and states that he would not treat the choice as lopsided. Eriksson ranked it second at opening and Kroll and Johansson would put it later, so the minority position is a disagreement about maturity and credit, not about the importance of the field.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members ranked B052 at opening and all eight round-1 files either prefer it (seven) or list it as an alternative (Mehlig); no member states a scientific objection to the lattice-clock results themselves.

Everyone who addresses B052 names Katori and Ye as the principal originators: Katori for the magic-wavelength proposal and first strontium lattice demonstration, Ye for record accuracy, coherence and many-body operation.

B010 (ATLAS/CMS Higgs) is treated as a very important discovery, but Danielsson, Olsson, Mehlig, Johansson, Lindroth and Pearce all state that Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as named individuals do not map cleanly onto those who made the 2012 observation. Danielsson, its original first-place proponent, now lists it only as an alternative.

B056 (circuit QED) is not in any configuration. Johansson, who ranked it first at opening, withdrew it himself over timing relative to the 2025 prize and the omission of Blais under a three-person cap.

Several members want any B052 citation tied to the lattice clock itself, not to precision spectroscopy in general, so that it neither repeats the 2005 comb prize nor pre-empts later work on a thorium nuclear clock.
scientific_disputes: Discovery or instrument: Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Olsson, Pearce and Mehlig all raise that a lattice-clock prize could be read as a refinement of metrology rather than a discovery. Replies in the files are that magic-wavelength many-atom interrogation is a distinct physical idea from the frequency comb (Lindroth, Johansson, Eriksson, Pearce), while Mehlig and Eriksson note that the fundamental-physics payoff (constants, dark matter) is still largely prospective.

Whether the opening of a new regime justifies the prize, or whether precedent (2005, 1989, 2012) should be used as an argument at all. Johansson, Eriksson and Olsson explicitly caution against relying on tradition.

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism and device variability in B024 make the discovery premature (Eriksson, Kroll, Johansson, Olsson, Pearce) or are separable from the robust flat-band correlated phases (Mehlig).

Whether a verified new state of matter (B021, B024) is a stronger kind of discovery than a measurement technique; Eriksson and Mehlig lean to this view in principle but both ranked B052 above B021 in their configurations or alternatives.
Lindroth, Kroll and Johansson treat B035 (atom interferometry) as the natural precision-measurement companion, but all three decline to make it a second prize part now.
attribution_disputes: B052: Olsson asks whether Ye's contribution is an original and decisive step or an improvement of Katori's invention, and wants the record to show which JILA results are Ye's own versus those of Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom and others. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce name further claimants (Lemonde and SYRTE, Lisdat, Takamoto, Yb, Hg and Al+ groups) but regard the Katori-Ye pairing as defensible. Several flag that priority details were recalled from memory, not verified.
B010: the credited trio are described as founders and programme leaders, not the 2012 spokespersons, trigger and analysis leaders; no member offers a three-name set they regard as fair.

B024: Cao as first author of the 2018 papers, the earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto theory, and the Dean, Young, Yazdani and Kim groups are outside the three names; Bistritzer and MacDonald share one theory paper.
B021: Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan and the three-dimensional work lie outside Kane, Mele and Molenkamp (Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce).
B043: the AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND pioneers are not in the Halzen and Spiering credit (Danielsson, Kroll, Johansson, Lindroth, Pearce).
B035: Chu's absence, given the 1997 prize, and the Bordé, Pritchard, Kasevich and Mlynek-type early demonstrations make the trio contested (Kroll, Lindroth, Eriksson, Pearce).
B011: Olsson raises the STEM corrector line of Krivanek and collaborators against the TEM correctors of Rose, Haider and Urban; no other member has assessed it.
maturity_disputes: B043 (IceCube): the diffuse astrophysical flux is accepted as established, but Danielsson, Kroll, Johansson, Lindroth and Pearce note that source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) rest on few objects at moderate significance. Danielsson and Johansson see B043 as a strong later candidate; Pearce keeps it as his alternative.
B024: experiments are eight years old, pairing is unexplained and samples vary; Mehlig regards the phase existence as already robust.

B052: maturity is the one dimension on which members agree it is strong, but the pending redefinition of the SI second is regarded by Johansson, Olsson and Kroll as not a scientific criterion, with Kroll noting it has not yet happened; Eriksson asks whether Ye's possible later nuclear-clock credit should affect timing.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and a Chalmers superconducting-circuit theorist, close to B056; states he would recuse on B056 if it became live. B056 is currently in no member's configuration.

Olsson: works in transmission electron microscopy and is President of the International Federation of Societies for Microscopy, so advocacy for B011 may be seen as biased; she invites weighing or recusal on that ballot.
Danielsson: his horizonless black-hole mimicker work lies close to B041 (Event Horizon Telescope); he would raise it if it came to a vote. B041 is not in any round-1 configuration.
Kroll: executive management of WACQT, Chalmers-led and institutionally overlapping with Johansson; relevant to B056 and B044, not to B052.
Lindroth: long-time collaborator of 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier and in adjacent atomic theory; no tie to any credited name on a shortlisted ballot she puts forward.
Mehlig: same Gothenburg environment as Johansson and Olsson, institutional only.

Pearce (chair): field proximity to B043 (IceCube) and B041 (EHT) as an experimental astroparticle and astrophysics researcher, with no listed collaboration with those teams; no recorded connection to Katori or Ye. Eriksson reports no conflict on the shortlist.
questions_for_round2: Olsson: what evidence in the record establishes that Ye's contribution is original and decisive in its own right, as distinct from taking Katori's lattice clock to record accuracy, and can Johansson, Lindroth and Kroll point to specific results (the JILA strontium lattice work, many-body and Fermi-degenerate operation) that separate the two roles in a citation?

What citation wording for B052 should the committee test: one that names the lattice clock and magic-wavelength trapping explicitly, so it neither duplicates the 2005 comb prize nor pre-empts a nuclear-clock recognition, or broader precision-measurement wording? Do members still hold that wording problems are a drafting matter and not a bar?

Mehlig: given that the case for B052 is clean on attribution and replication, what specific new evidence, citation, or attribution rule would be needed for B024 to be preferred to B052 this year, and does his preference rest on discovery type or on maturity?

Is there any member who would make a two-part prize of B052 with another ballot (B043, B035, B024, B021) and, if so, which three people in total? Kroll and Lindroth currently decline B035, and Pearce notes B043 would require trimming credited names.

For B043, does any member now regard the source associations as mature enough this year, and how should the AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND pioneers be handled if the committee returns to it in a later round?

Olsson asks to be heard on B011: can the Krivanek STEM-corrector line be handled by citation wording around TEM aberration correction, and should her conflict note change how colleagues weigh a ballot only she ranked?

For B010, is there a three-name or organisational formulation for the ATLAS and CMS discovery that members could regard as faithful to the record, or is it excluded from this year's discussion by the attribution problem?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows seven single-part configurations on B052 and one on B024, with B052 also an alternative for the B024 proponent. This is a narrower convergence than the opening rankings, and several members say they moved after reading colleagues, so it should not be read as seven independent judgements. The residual questions concern Ye's separate credit, the overlap with earlier metrology prizes, and whether any second prize part can be assembled without creating attribution problems, not the scientific correctness of the lattice-clock results. I note that I moved from IceCube first to B052 and that atomic physics is outside my own expertise; round 2 should test the B052 case with the AMO members rather than rely on my reading.
